chapter: Cliff Jackson, Jelly Roll Morton and Harlem in the 1920s
title: Tricking trumpeters by playing in hard keys
summary: The Carter and Jackson crowd tested a newcomer at the dance corner by playing through every key.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: I said, what kind of name is that? Cliff said, well, we want to trick a guy. That was a funny thing in New York years ago, Benny and all of us --

-- Benny Carter and Jimmy Harris (or) trombone player, so we'd go down to the dance corner on East 14th Street. What happened, Say hey fellow (unintelligible) -- they got a guy in town, man, he was a hell of a trumpet player. Said, yeah? Yeah. Well, what does he play? Everything. Said, bring him on down. So the trick was they started off in the key of C, keep (unintelligible) on up. go through (Unintelligible) all the keys. If the fellow fall out, get in them big keys (unintelligible).
like the pianos chatters in E majors, you know, or like the B natural Jimmy said -- Benny said (unintelligible). I said, right, he's playing them keys, man. (Unintelligible) --
-- because you couldn't keep up, that was it. He loved to trick the guys, you know. New York was really a tough place, because we could knock out the -- Hawk and (unintelligible) --
